prompt.context: Your client is Royal Honey, a manufacturer of premium organic honey that purchases its raw honey from a single farm in the Midwest. Despite record-high demand for high-quality organic honey nationwide, Royal Honey has experienced a gradual decline in profitability in recent years. Its CEO has come to you to determine why the company's financial state has rapidly deteriorated over the past four years and to develop a turnaround strategy for the company. The overall goal is to return the company to FY16 profitability within two years. Royal Honey sells only one product: organic golden honey. It purchases raw honey from suppliers, manufactures organic golden honey, and sells to domestic high-end grocery stores (e.g., Whole Foods) nationwide. Declining revenue and profitability have also been observed across all major competitors, though not to the same extent as Royal Honey.
prompt.question: Why has Royal Honey's financial state rapidly deteriorated over the past four years, and what turnaround strategy would you recommend to return the company to FY16 profitability within two years?

clarifying_info.q: What is Royal Honey's selling price?
clarifying_info.a: The selling price has remained consistent at $10 per pound.

clarifying_info.q: What does cost of goods include?
clarifying_info.a: Cost of goods includes raw honey, processing, manufacturing, bottling, and labeling.

clarifying_info.q: Does Royal Honey have any minimum purchase obligations with its current supplier?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, Royal Honey has a minimum purchase order of 10M pounds annually with its Midwest supplier.

exhibits.title: Royal Honey Revenue and Expenses FY16–FY19
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing Royal Honey's annual revenue and cost breakdown (Cost of Goods, Sales and Marketing, Overhead, Other) for FY16, FY17, FY18, and FY19 in $ millions.

exhibits.title: Total Domestic Supply of Raw Honey by Region FY16–FY19
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the total domestic supply of raw honey (value of production in $ millions) broken down by region (Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, Southwest, West) for FY16, FY17, FY18, and FY19.

data.note: Midwest has declined approximately $120M over the four-year period; other regions show smaller declines.

exhibits.title: Potential Raw Honey Suppliers
exhibits.shows: A table listing Royal Honey's current supplier and four international alternative suppliers, with available raw honey supply (lbs), raw honey cost per pound, and other cost considerations per pound (transportation, manufacturing, SG&A, etc.).

framework: Raw Honey Procurement — supplier concentration risk, pricing trends, supply availability
Honey Manufacturing/Processing (Operations) — production efficiency, capacity utilization
Distribution/Sales — channel mix, volume trends, pricing
Honey Market Analysis — new entrants, demand shifts (food vs. consumer goods), honeybee population decline, FDA regulations
Revenue/Cost Analysis — price and volume changes over time

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about Royal Honey's financial performance, and what follow-on questions does it raise?
questions.guidance: Strong candidate should identify: (1) Revenue has declined $30M over four years (from $210M to $180M); profits have declined $25M (from $30M to $5M). (2) Total expenses have remained relatively stable in dollar terms (~$180M), but have risen significantly as a percent of revenue. (3) To meet the goal of returning to FY16 profit ($30M), Royal Honey needs to increase profit by $25M by FY21. (4) Since price is stable at $10/lb, declining revenue implies declining sales volume. Candidate should ask about cost of goods detail and sales volume trends, which triggers Exhibit 2.

math.setup: Implied profit = Revenue minus total costs. FY16: $210M - ($120M+$30M+$20M+$10M) = $30M. FY19: $180M - ($120M+$25M+$20M+$10M) = $5M. Revenue decline = $210M - $180M = $30M. Profit decline = $30M - $5M = $25M. Gap to close = $25M.
math.answer: Profit has declined $25M; volume has declined 3M lbs; need $25M more profit by FY21

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 2 reveal about Royal Honey's supply situation, and what are the strategic implications?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) Total domestic honey production has declined ~$200M over four years. (2) The Midwest has been most affected, declining ~$120M (from ~$620M to ~$500M). (3) Declining supply drives up raw honey prices. Since Royal Honey sources exclusively from a single Midwest farm, it faces both supply constraints (unable to meet demand) and rising input costs. A strong candidate will connect supply constraints to lost revenue and note the need to explore international sourcing.

math.setup: Midwest production decline: $620M to $500M = -$120M. Total decline approximately -$200M.
steps: Midwest share of decline = $120M / $200M = 60% of total decline
math.answer: Midwest accounts for ~60% of total domestic production decline, directly impacting Royal Honey's single-source supplier

questions.prompt: Given demand of 30M lbs in FY21 and a sale price of $10/lb, what is the optimal raw honey procurement strategy to maximize profit? (Exhibit 3)
questions.guidance: Candidate should rank suppliers by profit per pound (revenue minus total cost per pound), then fill demand starting from the highest-margin supplier, subject to available supply and the minimum 10M lb purchase obligation with the current supplier. Without minimum purchase constraint: prioritize China+S.Africa (5M+5M lbs at $2/lb), then Mexico (10M lbs at $1/lb), then Brazil (10M lbs at $0.50/lb) = $35M profit. With minimum purchase constraint of 10M lbs from current supplier, displace 10M lbs of Brazil sourcing with 10M lbs of Current: profit = $32.5M. Strong candidates will ask about existing contract terms and surface the constraint.

math.setup: Profit per lb = $10 selling price minus total cost per lb. Rank by profit per lb, fill 30M lbs of demand from cheapest first. Check minimum purchase order constraint.
steps: Unconstrained optimal: China 5M lbs + S.Africa 5M lbs + Mexico 10M lbs + Brazil 10M lbs = 30M lbs
Unconstrained profit: (5M x $2) + (5M x $2) + (10M x $1) + (10M x $0.50) = $10M + $10M + $10M + $5M = $35M
Constrained (10M lb minimum with current supplier): China 5M + S.Africa 5M + Mexico 10M + Current 10M = 30M lbs
$32.5M profit exceeds FY16 goal of $30M by $2.5M (8.3%)
math.answer: With minimum purchase constraint: $32.5M profit, exceeding FY16 goal of $30M by $2.5M (8.3%)

brainstorming.prompt: For the past few years, honeybee populations in the United States have been declining. This has resulted in limited availability of raw honey as well as rising prices. This trend has especially impacted Royal Honey as its Midwest supplier has declining raw honey production and has increased its price annually. Given this information, what should Royal Honey consider to increase profitability?

categories.name: Procurement Expansion
ideas: Expand procurement beyond single Midwest farm to source raw honey internationally (e.g., Mexico, South America)
Vertically integrate or partner internationally with overseas honey producers
Diversify supplier base domestically across multiple regions to reduce concentration risk

categories.name: Product & R&D Innovation
ideas: Invest in R&D to develop an animal-free (lab-grown) honey product
Invest in R&D to develop sustainable practices and technologies that better preserve beehive populations
Adjust the formulation/mixture of Royal Honey to utilize less raw honey per unit, expanding achievable volume

categories.name: Pricing & Revenue
ideas: Raise the retail price of honey sold at stores to offset rising input costs
Explore premium product tiers or product line extensions

categories.name: Risks & Challenges to Highlight
ideas: Complexity of establishing new international supply agreements
Additional costs and logistics of international supply chains (transportation, duties)
International taxes, trade agreements, and tariffs
Potential FDA regulatory requirements for imported honey
Quality control challenges with new suppliers

recommendation: Expand raw honey procurement internationally, prioritizing China and South Africa (5M lbs each at $2/lb margin), then Mexico (10M lbs at $1/lb margin), while fulfilling the minimum 10M lb contract with the current Midwest supplier (at $0.25/lb margin)
This procurement strategy yields $32.5M in net income in FY21, exceeding the FY16 profitability goal of $30M by $2.5M (8.3%)
risks: Complexity and lead time in establishing new international supply chains
FDA regulatory compliance requirements for imported honey
Competitor response to Royal Honey's expanded supply capacity
Changing customer preferences or demand levels
Continued decline of domestic and global honeybee populations
Quality control and consistency challenges with new international suppliers
next_steps: Perform due diligence on international supplier candidates (China, South Africa, Mexico) — assess quality, certifications, reliability
Negotiate and establish shipping and supply contracts with selected international suppliers
Expand production capacity (manufacturing, bottling, labeling) as needed to handle 30M lbs
Monitor honeybee population trends and develop a contingency sourcing plan
